statement: Maya timekeeping linked directly observed solar cycles to agricultural timing: observations of the Sun, including zenith passages and horizon positions, were used to organize seasonal and maize-growing cycles.

sources.citation: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Living Maya Time, “Sun, Corn, and the Calendar.”
sources.author: Smithsonian NMAI
sources.venue: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian

sources.citation: Susan Milbrath, “The Role of Solar Observations in Developing the Preclassic Maya Calendar,” Latin American Antiquity (2017).
sources.author: Susan Milbrath
sources.venue: Latin American Antiquity / Cambridge University Press

notes: Stored as a natural/observational explanatory-practice claim because seasonal planning is tied to recurring observable solar phenomena; this category does not imply Maya cosmology was secular.
